content.value_statement: Manual test case writing is slow and inconsistent across teams. This skill converts requirements into structured Excel-ready test cases with defined fields and coverage guidance.
actual_capabilities: Extracts functional points, business flows, inputs, outputs, rules, and edge cases from requirements.
Plans normal, boundary, exception, security, compatibility, and usability test coverage when applicable.
Generates test cases using a fixed 15-field structure and required field order.
Prepares Excel output with formatted headers, wrapping, borders, and adjusted column widths.
Asks up to five clarification questions when requirements lack testable details.
Summarizes generated case counts, priority distribution, and covered functional areas.
limitations: Output quality depends on complete and accurate requirement documents.
It cannot verify actual system behavior without access to the running product.
Excel generation requires a Python environment with openpyxl available.
Image, PDF, and DOCX analysis depends on the host tool support for those files.

use_cases.title: Create Test Cases From Product Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn a feature specification into structured cases for normal, boundary, and exception flows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Acceptance Coverage For A Feature
use_cases.description: Check whether a requirement has enough verifiable cases before development starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Testing Documents Across Teams
use_cases.description: Generate consistent Excel-ready test case files that follow the same 15-field template.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single clear requirement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate functional test cases from this requirement. Use the 15-field format and create an Excel-ready result.

prompt_templates.title: Focus On Edge Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for stronger boundary and exception coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this requirement and generate test cases with normal, boundary, and exception scenarios. List any assumptions before creating the Excel file.

prompt_templates.title: Use Team Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with project-specific naming and priorities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate test cases for this feature. Apply our naming rules, assign high priority to payment and permission flows, and keep actual results blank.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for review before final output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this requirement for missing testable details. Ask up to five clarification questions, then generate Excel-ready cases after I answer.

output_examples.input: A login requirement with username, password, failed attempts, and remember-me behavior.
output: Excel-ready cases for successful login, invalid credentials, empty fields, account lockout, and remember-me behavior.
A summary with total cases, positive cases, exception cases, and covered login functions.

output_examples.input: A file upload requirement with allowed formats, size limits, and file name limits.
output: Cases for valid uploads, unsupported formats, maximum size, oversized files, and long file names.
Each case includes preconditions, steps, test data, expected results, type, status, priority, and creator.

output_examples.input: A short requirement that omits error messages and boundary rules.
output_examples.output: A short clarification list is produced first. If the user asks to continue, assumptions are listed with the generated cases.

best_practices: Provide clear business rules, validation rules, and expected error messages with the requirement.
State desired case count, priority rules, and any team naming conventions before generation.
Review assumptions and adjust generated cases before importing them into a test management system.
anti_patterns: Do not provide vague feature names without workflows, inputs, or expected outcomes.
Do not treat generated cases as executed test results or production validation evidence.
Do not skip review when requirements involve payments, permissions, privacy, or security controls.

faq.question: What input formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports text requirements, images, PDF files, and DOCX files when the host environment can read them.

faq.question: What does the Excel file contain?
faq.answer: It contains 15 ordered fields, including module, function, steps, test data, expected result, type, status, priority, and creator.

faq.question: Can it create security test cases?
faq.answer: Yes. It adds security cases for authentication, authorization, sensitive data, and access control when the requirement supports them.

faq.question: Will it ask questions before generating cases?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks up to five questions when missing details would reduce test quality or make cases hard to verify.

faq.question: Can I request a specific number of cases?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request an approximate count or ask for deeper coverage in selected modules.

faq.question: Does it execute the generated test cases?
faq.answer: No. It creates test case documentation. A tester or automation system must execute the cases separately.
